I'm an AI compiler engineer at [MediaTek](https://www.mediatek.com/). I work on the compiler for MDLA, MediaTek's on-device NPU, and spend most of my days figuring out how to make neural networks run faster and use less memory on it.

I came to compilers from computer vision. During my master's at NYCU I was in the [HCIS Lab](https://sites.google.com/site/yitingchen0524/hcis-lab), working on risk object identification for autonomous driving 🚗. That background still helps a lot. It's much easier to optimize a model when you know what it's actually doing.

### What I'm working on

- Hardware-aware optimizations in the MDLA compiler
- Tracking down NPU performance bottlenecks, and building a hint-guided option tuner to get better speed and memory usage
- Tools I use every day:
  ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-24292f?style=flat-square&logo=cplusplus&logoColor=white)
  ![MLIR](https://img.shields.io/badge/MLIR-24292f?style=flat-square&logo=llvm&logoColor=white)
  ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-24292f?style=flat-square&logo=tensorflow&logoColor=white)

I'm also really interested in generative AI on edge devices, and in how to make it fast enough to be useful in practice.
